1944-12-01.title: World War II Military Situation Maps, HQ Twelfth Army Group situation map [December 1, 1944]
1944-12-01.note: 1:1,000,000 outline map, a different print from October–November (shifted and extended to 52°N and 9°E); towns and bottom-edge ticks read on this scan; towns marked (from 1 Nov) placed by the 1 November model and carried over by SIFT/RANSAC homographies of the north-west and south-east of the sheet
1944-12-01.tail_note: South of the sheet's bottom edge: the southern rim of the Colmar pocket from Thann and Cernay to the Rhine above Mulhouse (Mulhouse taken 21 November, the Rhine reached at Rosenau 19 November 1944)
adjustments: Strasbourg: the line is drawn across the city's eastern edge on the Rhine; two points moved about 20 pixels (3 km) east onto the Rhine bank, since the city was taken on 23 November and the Kehl bridgehead on the west bank cleared by 25 November 1944, and the city centre would otherwise fall on the German side within the sheet's 1–2 km fit

1944-09-01.title: World War II Military Situation Maps, HQ Twelfth Army Group situation map [September 1, 1944]
1944-09-01.note: 1:750,000 sheet of the Seine–Paris sector; towns and the 30' ticks of the bottom edge read on this scan

front.note: The Amiens bridgehead: the line leaves the sheet's top edge north of Amiens and comes back east of it

No front line is drawn east of Amiens: the First and Third Armies' units stand at the sheet's right edge with arrows towards the Somme, the Aisne and the Meuse. Written after the histories (MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign; Blumenson, Breakout and Pursuit): St-Quentin and Laon (1 September), Rethel, the Meuse bridgeheads at Verdun and Commercy (31 August–1 September), and the Third Army's open southern flank from the Marne at Joinville past Troyes and Auxerre to the Loire
The Loire from Nevers to Saint-Nazaire: the north bank Allied (Orléans 16 August, Nantes 12 August, Tours 1 September), the south bank held by the retreating Army Group G until mid-September

1944-10-01.title: World War II Military Situation Maps, HQ Twelfth Army Group situation map [October 1, 1944]
1944-10-01.note: 1:1,000,000 outline map; towns and border ticks read on this scan (Bruges, Ghent and Breda read on the 1 November scan of the same print and carried back)

front.note: No front line is drawn on this sheet (the hatched bands are the West Wall). The line runs between the Allied and German unit symbols, placed through the sheet's model: the Breskens pocket behind the Leopold Canal; north of Antwerp between the 2nd Canadian, 49th and Polish divisions (51.36–51.39 N) and the German 711th, 719th and 245th (51.44–51.50 N) towards Turnhout; the west side of the Eindhoven–Nijmegen corridor; the Island between the Waal and the Neder Rijn; the east flank before the German 107th, 180th and 6th Parachute divisions west of the Maas (Overloon–Venray)

Twelfth and Sixth Army Groups, between the unit symbols: XIX Corps before Geilenkirchen, VII Corps between the two West Wall belts at Stolberg with Aachen still German, V Corps in the Schnee Eifel, the German border along the Our and the Sauer, XX Corps west of Thionville and Metz with the Arnaville bridgehead, XII Corps east of Nancy and Lunéville, XV Corps and the Seventh Army before the Vosges east of Épinal, the French First Army before Belfort
